A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ADU-Bench and contain readable main text, figures, tables, and appendices A–J. Sections and results can be matched reliably despite reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original evaluations of 13 LALMs, human preference studies, and experiments examining synthetic audio and evaluation-position bias.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds evaluations of three models and direct human ratings.

M1.justification: The benchmark construction and automated evaluation procedures remain unchanged: SSML-based synthesis, textual references, and LLM scoring averaged across reversed reference/response orders. Sections 3–4 and Appendices A–B introduce no new algorithm or model component.

E1.justification: Tables 1 and 8 retain the same datasets, sources, and domain counts: three general scenarios, twelve skills, nine languages, and four ambiguity types. The additional models and human ratings use existing benchmark coverage.

E2.justification: V2 expands the evaluated set from 13 to 16 models by adding Moshi-7B, Step-Audio-Chat-130B, and GPT-4o. Their participation is documented throughout Tables 2, 4–5, and 9–22, substantially extending comparisons to stronger audio-dialogue systems.

E3.justification: V2 adds direct 0–10 human scoring of 140 dialogues, with three raters per sample, while retaining the ten-tester pairwise study. Section 5.1 also changes the stated Whisper+GPT-4 backend from GPT-4-0613 to GPT-4 (gpt-4o-0613); whether this represents an actual configuration change or an identifier typo is unresolved.

E4.justification: Direct human ratings for five models add a complementary validation analysis in Table 2 and Appendix D. The existing model-size, real-versus-synthetic audio, pairwise-agreement, and position-bias analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seeds, repeated-run variability, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests. V2 adds human point scores without introducing uncertainty estimation; its wording about significantly higher correlation is not accompanied by a statistical test.

E6.justification: All 13 original models retain their numerical entries, while Tables 2, 4–5, and 9–22 add extensive results for three models. Table 2 reports averages of 2.94 for Moshi, 5.21 for Step-Audio-Chat, and 8.16 for GPT-4o, making GPT-4o the expanded comparison's leader; v1's leader was Whisper+GPT-4 at 7.66. Five direct human-score results are also added.

T1.justification: The operational dataset definitions and scoring rules remain unchanged. Neither version presents formal theorems, proofs, or substantive mathematical derivations.

C1.justification: Both versions claim a comprehensive four-part audio-dialogue benchmark, emphasize novelty in phonetic ambiguity evaluation, and identify the same headline model weaknesses. Evaluating 16 rather than 13 models expands supporting evidence without redefining these central contributions.

C2.justification: New Appendix E explains collection costs and conjectures that audio comprehension, rather than base-model reasoning, causes weak performance. Section 5.2 removes the blanket cascaded-model superiority conclusion and adds human-validation interpretation. The shortened limitations discussion omits v1's specific future adversarial, backdoor, and resource-manipulation evaluations.

D1.justification: V1 promises a future release; v2 supplies a project-page address and states that code and data are provided there. V2 also specifies the GPT-4o audio-preview version and documents the new human-rating instructions. Existing synthesis recipes, hardware descriptions, and evaluator prompts are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially revises benchmark positioning through a three-category taxonomy and explicit discussion of existing audio-dialogue benchmarks SD-Eval and VoiceBench. It also adds Dynamic-SUPERB Phase-2, Audio Entailment, MMAU, and AudioBench, while removing several earlier speech-corpus and security references.

P1.justification: V2 locally rewrites the abstract, introduction, related work, and conclusion, and divides Section 3 into Overall and Data Construction. It adds discussion and reproducibility appendices, shortens and relocates limitations, and moves Broader Impacts into a main-text Ethics Statement. Most exposition and the overall section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 2 gains a human-evaluation column and additional model rows; other result tables expand similarly. Figure 2 updates its radar plots and legend for 16 models, and appendix tables reflow across pages. Figures 1, 3, and 4 retain their visual content.

improvement.justification: The expanded model comparisons, especially GPT-4o, and complementary human ratings improve empirical relevance and validation. Closer prior-benchmark positioning and reported code/data access also help. These gains are limited by incompletely updated interpretation: Section 5.2 still calls BLSP best despite Step-Audio-Chat scoring 5.21 versus 3.85, and claims significantly higher human correlation without reporting a coefficient or test.
